page.text:
A function is the mathematical embodiment of a deterministic
transformation, assigning to each input exactly one output. Historically
conceived by Euler and Lagrange as symbolic algebraic formulas, the
modern conception was revolutionized by Peter Gustav Lejeune Dirichlet
and Richard Dedekind: a function $f : A \to B$ is an arbitrary rule of
association, requiring neither analytic formula nor geometric continuity.

In axiomatic set theory, a function is formally defined as a special kind
of binary relation: a subset of the Cartesian product $A \times B$
satisfying the dual requirements of existence (every domain element
$x \in A$ has an image) and uniqueness (no domain element is assigned
more than one image). Functions, and the binary operations that
specialize them, constitute the dynamic machinery through which algebraic
structures, topological spaces, and analytical dynamics are investigated.
